Alphabet introduced 'Google Cloud' as a distinct reportable segment starting with its Q4/FY2020 earnings release (filed 2021-02-02), which recast Q4 2019 and FY2018-2020 as comparatives. Individual Q1-Q3 2019 and all 2018 quarters are NOT available at quarterly granularity (only annual totals were disclosed for those periods) -- left as gaps, not estimated. Before this reorg, cloud revenue was bundled inside 'Google other revenues'.
No further Google Cloud segment redefinition found through FY2025 10-K (GCP + Google Workspace consistently).

3-segment structure (Productivity and Business Processes / Intelligent Cloud / More Personal Computing) began FY2016 Q1 (quarter ended Sep 30, 2015), replacing the prior 'Devices and Consumer'/'Commercial' structure used through FY2015. No 'Intelligent Cloud' figure exists for FY2015 or earlier -- confirmed by checking FY2015 earnings releases directly (they report only a qualitative 'Commercial cloud revenue' growth-rate metric, not a segment dollar figure).

Minor restatement: ASC 606 revenue-recognition standard adopted 2017-07-01 (FY2018). Originally reported (FY2017 Q1 own release, 2016-10-20): $6,382M. Recast (used here, shown as prior-year comparative in FY2018 Q1 release): $6,097M (-4.5%), source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000789019/000119312517321202/d483053dex991.htm, released 2017-10-26.

Microsoft's FY2023 Q1 release recast the FY2022 Q1 prior-year comparative from $16,964M (as originally reported in the FY2022 Q1 release) to $16,912M (-0.3%), per a 'we have recast certain prior period amounts to conform to the current period presentation' note in that filing. This row uses $20,325M, the figure AS ORIGINALLY REPORTED in MSFT's own FY2023 Q1 release (not a later recast of this quarter).

IMPORTANT FORWARD LIMITATION: on 2026-09-02 Microsoft announced that starting fiscal year 2027 (i.e. the quarter ending Sep 30, 2026, not yet reported as of this research) it is dropping the 3-segment structure entirely in favor of two new segments, 'Agents and Infra' and 'Devices and Consumer', and will begin disclosing Azure revenue in dollars directly. The 'Intelligent Cloud' series therefore cannot be extended past FY2026 Q4 under this definition; any later cloud-revenue proxy for MSFT will need to use the new segment structure, which is not comparable without further mapping work.
